items.name: autoemit_temperature_commands
items.label: Emit temperature commands automatically
items.tooltip:
When enabled, PrusaSlicer will check whether your custom Start G-code contains G-codes to set extruder, bed or chamber temperature (M104, M109, M140, M190, M141 and M191). If so, the temperatures will not be emitted automatically so you're free to customize the order of heating commands and other custom actions. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all PrusaSlicer settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.
If your custom Start G-code does NOT contain these G-codes, PrusaSlicer will execute the Start G-code after heated chamber was set to its temperature, bed reached its target temperature and extruder just started heating.

When disabled, PrusaSlicer will NOT emit commands to heat up extruder, bed or chamber, leaving all to Custom Start G-code.

items.name: before_layer_gcode
items.label: Before layer change G-code
items.tooltip: This custom code is inserted at every layer change, right before the Z move. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings as well as [layer_num] and [layer_z].

items.name: between_objects_gcode
items.label: Between objects G-code
items.tooltip: This code is inserted between objects when using sequential printing. By default extruder and bed temperature are reset using non-wait command; however if M104, M109, M140 or M190 are detected in this custom code, Slic3r will not add temperature commands. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.

items.name: binary_gcode
items.label: Supports binary G-code
items.tooltip: Enable, if the firmware supports binary G-code format (bgcode). To generate .bgcode files, make sure you have binary G-code enabled in Configuration->Preferences->Other.

items.name: color_change_gcode
items.label: Color change G-code
items.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the color change

items.name: cooling_tube_length
items.label: Cooling tube length
items.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

items.name: cooling_tube_retraction
items.label: Cooling tube position
items.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

items.name: custom_parameters_printer
items.label: Custom printer parameters
items.tooltip:
JSON-encoded string defining extra parameters, which can later be expanded in Custom G-code macro language. Each of the parameters is prepended by custom_parameter_printer prefix before it is passed into the parser. For example, defining '{"my_key": "my_value"}' allows to use 'custom_parameter_printer_my_key'.

The JSON must be single level (no arrays and objects). All value types are allowed, but nulls will be rejected by the parser.

items.name: default_print
items.label: Default Print Preset
items.tooltip: Name or ID of print preset to use as default when this printer preset is selected.

items.name: enable_pressure_advance_during_ramming
items.label: Enable pressure advance during ramming
items.tooltip: Check to enable pressure advance during ramming.

items.name: end_gcode
items.label: End G-code
items.tooltip: This end procedure is inserted at the end of the output file. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all PrusaSlicer settings.
items.value:
M104 S0 ; turn off temperature
G28 X0  ; home X axis
M84     ; disable motors

items.name: extra_loading_move
items.label: Extra loading distance
items.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further,  if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

items.name: extruder_clearance_height
items.label: Height
items.tooltip:
Only used when 'Print Settings -> Complete individual objects' is active. Set this to the vertical distance between your nozzle tip and (usually) the X carriage rods. Used to check for collisions with previously printed objects and to prevent them when arranging.
The value is ignored for most Prusa printers, which come with more detailed extruder model.

items.name: extruder_clearance_radius
items.label: Radius
items.tooltip:
Only used when 'Print Settings -> Complete individual objects' is active. Set this to a radius of a nozzle-centered cylinder big enough to enclose the extruder assembly. Used to check for collisions with previously printed objects and to prevent them when arranging.
The value is ignored for most Prusa printers, which come with more detailed extruder model.

items.name: extruder_offset
items.label: Extruder offset
items.tooltip: If your firmware doesn't handle the extruder displacement you need the G-code to take it into account. This option lets you specify the displacement of each extruder with respect to the first one. It expects positive coordinates (they will be subtracted from the XY coordinate).

items.name: filament_change_time
items.label: Filament change time
items.tooltip: Time required for a single filament change. On a printer with multiple tools this is the time required for a single toolchange to take place. On a printer with multi-material upgrade, this is the time required to unload and load a new filament.

items.name: gcode_flavor
items.label: G-code flavor
items.tooltip: Some G/M-code commands, including temperature control and others, are not universal. Set this option to your printer's firmware to get a compatible output. The "No extrusion" flavor prevents PrusaSlicer from exporting any extrusion value at all.

items.name: high_current_on_filament_swap
items.label: High extruder current on filament swap
items.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

items.name: layer_gcode
items.label: After layer change G-code
items.tooltip: This custom code is inserted at every layer change, right after the Z move and before the extruder moves to the first layer point. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings as well as [layer_num] and [layer_z].

items.label: Max print height
items.tooltip: Set this to the maximum height that can be reached by your extruder while printing.

items.name: multimaterial_purging
items.label: Purging volume
items.tooltip: Determines purging volume on the wipe tower. This can be modified in Filament Settings ('filament_purge_multiplier') or overridden using project-specific settings.

items.name: parking_pos_retraction
items.label: Filament parking position
items.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

items.label: Pause Print G-code
items.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print

items.label: Prefer clockwise movements
items.tooltip: This setting makes the printer print loops clockwise instead of counterclockwise.

items.label: Printer variant
items.tooltip: Name of the printer variant. For example, the printer variants may be differentiated by a nozzle diameter.

items.label: Printer vendor
items.tooltip: Name of the printer vendor.

items.name: remaining_times
items.label: Supports remaining times
items.tooltip: Emit M73 P[percent printed] R[remaining time in minutes] at 1 minute intervals into the G-code to let the firmware show accurate remaining time. As of now only the Prusa i3 MK3 firmware recognizes M73. Also the i3 MK3 firmware supports M73 Qxx Sxx for the silent mode.

items.tooltip: The firmware supports stealth mode

items.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
items.tooltip: The printer multiplexes filaments into a single hot end.

items.label: Start G-code
items.tooltip: This start procedure is inserted at the beginning, possibly prepended by temperature-changing commands. See 'autoemit_temperature_commands'.

G1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle

items.name: stuck_filament_detection
items.label: Supports stuck filament monitoring configuration
items.tooltip: Enable, if the firmware supports configuring the stuck filament detection via the M591 gcode.

items.name: template_custom_gcode
items.label: Custom G-code
items.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code

items.name: thumbnails
items.label: G-code thumbnails
items.tooltip:
Picture sizes to be stored in .gcode / .bgcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY/EXT, XxY/EXT, ..."
Currently supported extensions are PNG, QOI and JPG.

items.name: thumbnails_format
items.label: Format of G-code thumbnails
items.tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware

items.name: toolchange_gcode
items.label: Tool change G-code
items.tooltip: This custom code is inserted before every toolchange. Placeholder variables for all PrusaSlicer settings as well as {toolchange_z}, {previous_extruder} and {next_extruder} can be used. When a tool-changing command which changes to the correct extruder is included (such as T{next_extruder}), PrusaSlicer will emit no other such command. It is therefore possible to script custom behaviour both before and after the toolchange.

items.name: use_firmware_retraction
items.label: Use firmware retraction
items.tooltip: This setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. Note that this has to be supported by firmware.

items.name: use_relative_e_distances
items.label: Use relative E distances
items.tooltip: If your firmware requires relative E values, check this, otherwise leave it unchecked. Most firmwares use absolute values.

items.name: use_volumetric_e
items.label: Use volumetric E
items.tooltip: This experimental setting uses outputs the E values in cubic millimeters instead of linear millimeters. If your firmware doesn't already know filament diameter(s), you can put commands like 'M200 D[filament_diameter_0] T0' in your start G-code in order to turn volumetric mode on and use the filament diameter associated to the filament selected in Slic3r. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

items.name: variable_layer_height
items.label: Enable variable layer height feature
items.tooltip: Some printers or printer setups may have difficulties printing with a variable layer height. Enabled by default.

items.name: z_offset
items.label: Z offset
items.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

items.name: arc_fitting
items.label: Arc fitting
items.tooltip: Enable to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. G-code resolution will be used as the fitting tolerance.

items.name: automatic_extrusion_widths
items.label: Automatic extrusion widths calculation
items.tooltip: Automatically calculates extrusion widths based on the nozzle diameter of the currently used extruder. This setting is essential for printing with different nozzle diameters.

items.name: automatic_infill_combination
items.label: Automatic infill combination
items.tooltip: This feature automatically combines infill of several layers and speeds up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus maintaining accuracy.

items.name: automatic_infill_combination_max_layer_height
items.label: Automatic infill combination - Max layer height
items.tooltip: Maximum layer height for combining infill when automatic infill combining is enabled. Maximum layer height could be specified either as an absolute in millimeters value or as a percentage of nozzle diameter. For printing with different nozzle diameters, it is recommended to use percentage value over absolute value.

items.name: avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs
items.label: Avoid crossing curled overhangs (Experimental)
items.tooltip: Plan travel moves such that the extruder avoids areas where the filament may be curled up. This is mostly happening on steeper rounded overhangs and may cause a crash with the nozzle. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

items.name: avoid_crossing_perimeters
items.label: Avoid crossing perimeters
items.tooltip: Optimize travel moves in order to minimize the crossing of perimeters. This is mostly useful with Bowden extruders which suffer from oozing. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

items.name: avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour
items.label: Avoid crossing perimeters - Max detour length
items.tooltip: The maximum detour length for avoid crossing perimeters. If the detour is longer than this value, avoid crossing perimeters is not applied for this travel path.

items.name: bed_temperature_extruder
items.label: Bed temperature by extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder which determines bed temperatures. Set to 0 to determine temperatures based on the first printing extruder of the first and the second layers.

items.name: bottom_fill_pattern
items.label: Bottom fill pattern
items.tooltip: Fill pattern for bottom infill. This only affects the bottom external visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

items.name: bottom_solid_layers
items.label: Bottom solid layers
items.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on bottom surfaces.

items.name: bottom_solid_min_thickness
items.label: Minimum bottom shell thickness
items.tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased above bottom_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of bottom shell.

items.name: bridge_acceleration
items.label: Bridge
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for bridges. Set zero to disable acceleration control for bridges.

items.name: bridge_angle
items.label: Bridging angle
items.tooltip: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for all bridges. Use 180° for zero angle.

items.name: bridge_flow_ratio
items.label: Bridge flow ratio
items.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of plastic for bridging. You can decrease it slightly to pull the extrudates and prevent sagging, although default settings are usually good and you should experiment with cooling (use a fan) before tweaking this.

items.name: bridge_speed
items.label: Bridges
items.tooltip: Speed for printing bridges.

items.name: brim_separation
items.label: Brim separation gap
items.tooltip: Offset of brim from the printed object. The offset is applied after the elephant foot compensation.

items.name: brim_type
items.label: Brim type
items.tooltip: The places where the brim will be printed around each object on the first layer.

items.name: brim_width
items.label: Brim width
items.tooltip: The horizontal width of the brim that will be printed around each object on the first layer. When raft is used, no brim is generated (use raft_first_layer_expansion).

items.name: complete_objects
items.label: Complete individual objects
items.tooltip: When printing multiple objects or copies, this feature will complete each object before moving onto next one (and starting it from its bottom layer). This feature is useful to avoid the risk of ruined prints. Slic3r should warn and prevent you from extruder collisions, but beware.

items.name: custom_parameters_print
items.label: Custom print parameters
items.tooltip:
JSON-encoded string defining extra parameters, which can later be expanded in Custom G-code macro language. Each of the parameters is prepended by custom_parameter_print prefix before it is passed into the parser. For example, defining '{"my_key": "my_value"}' allows to use 'custom_parameter_print_my_key'.

The JSON must be single level (no arrays and objects). All value types are allowed, but nulls will be rejected by the parser.

items.name: default_acceleration
items.label: Default
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will be reset to after the role-specific acceleration values are used (perimeter/infill). Set zero to prevent resetting acceleration at all.

items.name: default_material
items.label: Default Material Preset
items.tooltip: Name or ID of material preset to use as default when this print preset is selected.

items.name: default_tool_print
items.label: Default Tool Print Preset
items.tooltip: Name or ID of tool print preset to use as default when this print preset is selected.

items.name: deretract_speed
items.label: Deretraction Speed
items.tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

items.name: dont_support_bridges
items.label: Don't support bridges
items.tooltip: Experimental option for preventing support material from being generated under bridged areas.

items.name: draft_shield
items.label: Draft shield
items.tooltip:
With draft shield active, the skirt will be printed skirt_distance from the object, possibly intersecting brim.
Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object.
Limited = skirt is as tall as specified by skirt_height.
This is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft.

items.name: elefant_foot_compensation
items.label: Elephant foot compensation
items.tooltip: The first layer will be shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value to compensate for the 1st layer squish aka an Elephant Foot effect.

items.name: enable_dynamic_overhang_speeds
items.label: Enable dynamic overhang speeds
items.tooltip: This setting enables dynamic speed control on overhangs.

items.name: ensure_vertical_shell_thickness
items.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
items.tooltip: Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers).

items.name: external_perimeter_acceleration
items.label: External perimeters
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for external perimeters. Set zero to use the value for perimeters.

items.name: external_perimeter_extrusion_width
items.label: External perimeters
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for external perimeters. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%), it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: external_perimeter_speed
items.label: External perimeters
items.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of external perimeters (the visible ones). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

items.name: external_perimeters_first
items.label: External perimeters first
items.tooltip: Print contour perimeters from the outermost one to the innermost one instead of the default inverse order.

items.name: extra_perimeters
items.label: Extra perimeters if needed
items.tooltip: Add more perimeters when needed for avoiding gaps in sloping walls. Slic3r keeps adding perimeters, until more than 70% of the loop immediately above is supported.

items.name: extra_perimeters_on_overhangs
items.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs (Experimental)
items.tooltip: Detect overhang areas where bridges cannot be anchored, and fill them with extra perimeter paths. These paths are anchored to the nearby non-overhang area when possible.

items.name: extrusion_width
items.label: Default extrusion width
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to allow a manual extrusion width. If left to zero, Slic3r derives extrusion widths from the nozzle diameter (see the tooltips for perimeter extrusion width, infill extrusion width etc). If expressed as percentage (for example: 230%), it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: fill_angle
items.label: Fill angle
items.tooltip: Default base angle for infill orientation. Cross-hatching will be applied to this. Bridges will be infilled using the best direction Slic3r can detect, so this setting does not affect them.

items.name: fill_density
items.label: Fill density
items.tooltip: Density of internal infill, expressed in the range 0% - 100%.

items.name: fill_pattern
items.label: Fill pattern
items.tooltip: Fill pattern for general low-density infill.

items.name: first_layer_acceleration
items.label: First layer
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer.

items.name: first_layer_acceleration_over_raft
items.label: First object layer over raft interface
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer of object above raft interface. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer of object above raft interface.

items.name: first_layer_external_perimeter_speed
items.label: First layer perimeter speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the external perimeter print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the external perimeter speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: first_layer_extrusion_width
items.label: First layer
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for first layer. You can use this to force fatter extrudates for better adhesion. If expressed as percentage (for example 120%) it will be computed over nozzle_diameter. If set to zero, it will use the default extrusion width.

items.name: first_layer_gap_fill_speed
items.label: First layer gap fill speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any gap fill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the gap fill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: first_layer_height
items.label: First layer height
items.tooltip: When printing with very low layer heights, you might still want to print a thicker bottom layer to improve adhesion and tolerance for non perfect build plates.

items.name: first_layer_infill_speed
items.label: First layer infill speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: first_layer_perimeter_speed
items.label: First layer perimeter speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the perimeter print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the perimeter speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: first_layer_solid_infill_speed
items.label: First layer solid infill speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the solid infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the solid infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: first_layer_speed
items.label: First layer speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first layer, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

items.name: first_layer_speed_over_raft
items.label: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first object layer above raft interface, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

items.name: first_layer_support_material_speed
items.label: First layer support material speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any support print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the support material speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: first_layer_top_solid_infill_speed
items.label: First layer top solid infill speed
items.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any top solid print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the top solid infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

items.name: fuzzy_skin
items.label: Fuzzy Skin
items.tooltip: Fuzzy skin type.

items.name: fuzzy_skin_point_dist
items.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
items.tooltip: Perimeters will be split into multiple segments by inserting Fuzzy skin points. Lowering the Fuzzy skin point distance will increase the number of randomly offset points on the perimeter wall.

items.name: fuzzy_skin_thickness
items.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
items.tooltip: The maximum distance that each skin point can be offset (both ways), measured perpendicular to the perimeter wall.

items.name: gap_fill_enabled
items.label: Fill gaps
items.tooltip: Enables filling of gaps between perimeters and between the inner most perimeters and infill.

items.name: gap_fill_speed
items.label: Gap fill
items.tooltip: Speed for filling small gaps using short zigzag moves. Keep this reasonably low to avoid too much shaking and resonance issues. Set zero to disable gaps filling.

items.name: gcode_comments
items.label: Verbose G-code
items.tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

items.name: gcode_label_objects
items.label: Label objects
items.tooltip:
Selects whether labels should be exported at object boundaries and in what format.
OctoPrint = comments to be consumed by OctoPrint CancelObject plugin.
Firmware = firmware specific G-code (it will be chosen based on firmware flavor and it can end up to be empty).

This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

items.name: gcode_resolution
items.label: G-code resolution
items.tooltip: Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts. Very high resolution G-code requires huge amount of RAM to slice and preview, also a 3D printer may stutter not being able to process a high resolution G-code in a timely manner. On the other hand, a low resolution G-code will produce a low poly effect and because the G-code reduction is performed at each layer independently, visible artifacts may be produced.

items.name: gcode_substitutions
items.label: G-code substitutions
items.tooltip: Find / replace patterns in G-code lines and substitute them.

items.name: infill_acceleration
items.label: Infill
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for infill. Set zero to disable acceleration control for infill.

items.name: infill_anchor
items.label: Length of the infill anchor
items.tooltip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. PrusaSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

items.name: infill_anchor_max
items.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
items.tooltip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. PrusaSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring.

items.name: infill_every_layers
items.label: Combine infill every
items.tooltip: This feature allows to combine infill and speed up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus accuracy.

items.name: infill_extruder
items.label: Infill extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing infill.

items.name: infill_extrusion_width
items.label: Infill
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. You may want to use fatter extrudates to speed up the infill and make your parts stronger. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: infill_first
items.label: Infill before perimeters
items.tooltip: This option will switch the print order of perimeters and infill, making the latter first.

items.name: infill_overlap
items.label: Infill/perimeters overlap
items.tooltip: This setting applies an additional overlap between infill and perimeters for better bonding. Theoretically this shouldn't be needed, but backlash might cause gaps. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over perimeter extrusion width.

items.name: infill_speed
items.label: Infill
items.tooltip: Speed for printing the internal fill. Set to zero for auto.

items.name: interface_shells
items.label: Interface shells
items.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

items.name: interlocking_beam
items.label: Use beam interlocking
items.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

items.name: interlocking_beam_layer_count
items.label: Interlocking beam layers
items.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

items.name: interlocking_beam_width
items.label: Interlocking beam width
items.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

items.name: interlocking_boundary_avoidance
items.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
items.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

items.name: interlocking_depth
items.label: Interlocking depth
items.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

items.name: interlocking_orientation
items.label: Interlocking direction
items.tooltip: Orientation of interlocking beams.

items.name: ironing
items.label: Enable ironing
items.tooltip: Enable ironing of the top layers with the hot print head for smooth surface

items.name: ironing_flowrate
items.label: Flow rate
items.tooltip: Percent of a flow rate relative to object's normal layer height.

items.name: ironing_spacing
items.label: Spacing between ironing passes
items.tooltip: Distance between ironing lines

items.name: ironing_speed
items.label: Ironing speed
items.tooltip: Ironing

items.name: ironing_type
items.label: Ironing Type
items.tooltip: Ironing Type

items.name: layer_height
items.label: Layer height
items.tooltip: This setting controls the height (and thus the total number) of the slices/layers. Thinner layers give better accuracy but take more time to print.

items.name: max_layer_height
items.label: Max
items.tooltip: This is the highest printable layer height for this extruder, used to cap the variable layer height and support layer height. Maximum recommended layer height is 75% of the extrusion width to achieve reasonable inter-layer adhesion. If set to 0, layer height is limited to 75% of the nozzle diameter.

items.name: max_print_speed
items.label: Max print speed
items.tooltip: When setting other speed settings to 0 Slic3r will autocalculate the optimal speed in order to keep constant extruder pressure. This experimental setting is used to set the highest print speed you want to allow.

items.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_negative
items.label: Max volumetric slope negative
items.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from higher speed to lower speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 5.4 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 60 mm/s) to 1.8 mm³/s (feedrate 20 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

items.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_positive
items.label: Max volumetric slope positive
items.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from lower speed to higher speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 1.8 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 20 mm/s) to 5.4 mm³/s (feedrate 60 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

items.name: max_volumetric_speed
items.label: Max volumetric speed
items.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to set the maximum volumetric speed your extruder supports.

items.name: min_bead_width
items.label: Minimum perimeter width
items.tooltip: Width of the perimeter that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum perimeter width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the perimeter will become as thick as the feature itself. If expressed as a percentage (for example 85%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

items.name: min_feature_size
items.label: Minimum feature size
items.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum perimeter width. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the biggest nozzle diameter.

items.name: min_layer_height
items.label: Min
items.tooltip: This is the lowest printable layer height for this extruder and limits the resolution for variable layer height. Typical values are between 0.05 mm and 0.1 mm.

items.name: min_skirt_length
items.label: Minimal filament extrusion length
items.tooltip: Generate no less than the number of skirt loops required to consume the specified amount of filament on the bottom layer. For multi-extruder machines, this minimum applies to each extruder.

items.name: mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth
items.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
items.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth"is bigger then "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

items.name: mmu_segmented_region_max_width
items.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
items.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. Zero disables this feature.

items.name: notes
items.label: Configuration notes
items.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

items.name: only_one_perimeter_first_layer
items.label: Only one perimeter on first layer
items.tooltip: Use only one perimeter on the first layer.

items.name: only_retract_when_crossing_perimeters
items.label: Only retract when crossing perimeters
items.tooltip: Disables retraction when the travel path does not exceed the upper layer's perimeters (and thus any ooze will be probably invisible).

items.name: ooze_prevention
items.label: Enable
items.tooltip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

items.name: output_filename_format
items.label: Output filename format
items.tooltip: You can use all configuration options as variables inside this template. For example: [layer_height], [fill_density] etc. You can also use [timestamp], [year], [month], [day], [hour], [minute], [second], [version], [input_filename_base], [default_output_extension].

items.name: over_bridge_speed
items.label: Over bridges
items.tooltip: Speed for printing solid infill above bridges. Set to 0 to use solid infill speed. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over solid infill speed.

items.name: overhang_speed_0
items.label: speed for 0% overlap (bridge)
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

items.name: overhang_speed_1
items.label: speed for 25% overlap
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

items.name: overhang_speed_2
items.label: speed for 50% overlap
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

items.name: overhang_speed_3
items.label: speed for 75% overlap
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

items.name: overhangs
items.label: Detect bridging perimeters
items.tooltip: Experimental option to adjust flow for overhangs (bridge flow will be used), to apply bridge speed to them and enable fan.

items.name: perimeter_acceleration
items.label: Perimeters
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for perimeters. Set zero to disable acceleration control for perimeters.

items.name: perimeter_extruder
items.label: Perimeter extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeters and brim. First extruder is 1.

items.name: perimeter_extrusion_width
items.label: Perimeters
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for perimeters. You may want to use thinner extrudates to get more accurate surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: perimeter_generator
items.label: Perimeter generator
items.tooltip: Classic perimeter generator produces perimeters with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces perimeters with variable extrusion width. This setting also affects the Concentric infill.

items.name: perimeter_speed
items.label: Perimeters
items.tooltip: Speed for perimeters (contours, aka vertical shells). Set to zero for auto.

items.name: perimeters
items.label: Perimeters
items.tooltip: This option sets the minimal number of perimeters to generate for each layer. Note that Slic3r may increase this number automatically when it detects sloping surfaces which benefit from a higher number of perimeters if the Extra Perimeters option is enabled.

items.name: post_process
items.label: Post-processing scripts
items.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Slic3r config settings by reading environment variables.

items.name: raft_contact_distance
items.label: Raft contact Z distance
items.tooltip: The vertical distance between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface.

items.name: raft_expansion
items.label: Raft expansion
items.tooltip: Expansion of the raft in XY plane for better stability.

items.name: raft_first_layer_density
items.label: First layer density
items.tooltip: Density of the first raft layer.

items.name: raft_first_layer_expansion
items.label: Raft first layer expansion
items.tooltip: Expansion of the raft first layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

items.name: raft_layers
items.label: Raft layers
items.tooltip: The object will be raised by this number of layers, and support material will be generated under it.

items.name: resolution
items.label: Slice resolution
items.tooltip: Minimum detail resolution, used to simplify the input file for speeding up the slicing job and reducing memory usage. High-resolution models often carry more detail than printers can render. Set to zero to disable any simplification and use full resolution from input.

items.name: retract_before_travel
items.label: Minimum travel after retraction
items.tooltip: Retraction is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

items.name: retract_before_wipe
items.label: Retract amount before wipe
items.tooltip: With bowden extruders, it may be wise to do some amount of quick retract before doing the wipe movement.

items.name: retract_layer_change
items.label: Retract on layer change
items.tooltip: This flag enforces a retraction whenever a Z move is done.

items.name: retract_length
items.label: Retraction length
items.tooltip: When retraction is triggered, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

items.name: retract_length_toolchange
items.label: Length
items.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

items.name: retract_lift
items.label: Lift height
items.tooltip: Lift height applied before travel.

items.name: retract_lift_above
items.label: Only lift Above Z
items.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for skipping lift on the first layers.

items.name: retract_lift_below
items.label: Only lift Below Z
items.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for limiting lift to the first layers.

items.name: retract_restart_extra
items.label: Deretraction extra length
items.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

items.name: retract_restart_extra_toolchange
items.label: Extra length on restart
items.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

items.name: retract_speed
items.label: Retraction Speed
items.tooltip: The speed for retractions (it only applies to the extruder motor).

items.name: scarf_seam_entire_loop
items.label: Scarf joint around entire perimeter
items.tooltip: Extend the scarf around entire length of the perimeter.

items.name: scarf_seam_length
items.label: Scarf joint length
items.tooltip: Length of the scarf joint.

items.name: scarf_seam_max_segment_length
items.label: Max scarf joint segment length
items.tooltip: Maximum length of any scarf joint segment.

items.name: scarf_seam_on_inner_perimeters
items.label: Scarf joint on inner perimeters
items.tooltip: Use scarf joint on inner perimeters.

items.name: scarf_seam_only_on_smooth
items.label: Scarf joint only on smooth perimeters
items.tooltip: Only use the scarf joint when the perimeter is smooth.

items.name: scarf_seam_placement
items.label: Scarf joint placement
items.tooltip: Where to place scarf joint seam.

items.name: scarf_seam_start_height
items.label: Scarf start height
items.tooltip: Start height of the scarf joint specified as fraction of the current layer height.

items.name: seam_gap_distance
items.label: Seam gap distance
items.tooltip: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.

items.name: seam_position
items.label: Seam position
items.tooltip: Position of perimeters starting points.

items.name: single_extruder_multi_material_priming
items.label: Prime all printing extruders
items.tooltip: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

items.name: skirt_distance
items.label: Distance from brim/object
items.tooltip: Distance between skirt and brim (when draft shield is not used) or objects.

items.name: skirt_height
items.label: Skirt height
items.tooltip: Height of skirt expressed in layers.

items.name: skirts
items.label: Loops (minimum)
items.tooltip: Number of loops for the skirt. If the Minimum Extrusion Length option is set, the number of loops might be greater than the one configured here. Set this to zero to disable skirt completely.

items.name: slice_closing_radius
items.label: Slice gap closing radius
items.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

items.name: slicing_mode
items.label: Slicing Mode
items.tooltip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

items.name: small_perimeter_speed
items.label: Small perimeters
items.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= 6.5mm (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

items.name: solid_infill_acceleration
items.label: Solid infill
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for solid infill. Set zero to use the value for infill.

items.name: solid_infill_below_area
items.label: Solid infill threshold area
items.tooltip: Force solid infill for regions having a smaller area than the specified threshold.

items.name: solid_infill_every_layers
items.label: Solid infill every
items.tooltip: This feature allows to force a solid layer every given number of layers. Zero to disable. You can set this to any value (for example 9999); Slic3r will automatically choose the maximum possible number of layers to combine according to nozzle diameter and layer height.

items.name: solid_infill_extruder
items.label: Solid infill extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing solid infill.

items.name: solid_infill_extrusion_width
items.label: Solid infill
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for solid surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: solid_infill_speed
items.label: Solid infill
items.tooltip: Speed for printing solid regions (top/bottom/internal horizontal shells). This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the default infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

items.name: spiral_vase
items.label: Spiral vase
items.tooltip: This feature will raise Z gradually while printing a single-walled object in order to remove any visible seam. This option requires a single perimeter, no infill, no top solid layers and no support material. You can still set any number of bottom solid layers as well as skirt/brim loops. It won't work when printing more than one single object.

items.name: staggered_inner_seams
items.label: Staggered inner seams
items.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

items.name: standby_temperature_delta
items.label: Temperature variation
items.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is defined.

items.name: support_material
items.label: Generate Supports
items.tooltip:
Enable support material generation.
Off - Disables support material generation.
Manual Only - Generates supports inside the "Support Enforcer" volumes only.
On - Generates supports automatically based on the overhang threshold value and also inside the "Support Enforcer" volumes.

items.name: support_material_angle
items.label: Pattern angle
items.tooltip: Use this setting to rotate the support material pattern on the horizontal plane.

items.name: support_material_bottom_contact_distance
items.label: Bottom contact Z distance
items.tooltip: The vertical distance between the object top surface and the support material interface. If set to zero, support_material_contact_distance will be used for both top and bottom contact Z distances.

items.name: support_material_bottom_interface_layers
items.label: Bottom interface layers
items.tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material. Set to -1 to use support_material_interface_layers

items.name: support_material_buildplate_only
items.label: Support on build plate only
items.tooltip: Only create support if it lies on a build plate. Don't create support on a print.

items.name: support_material_closing_radius
items.label: Closing radius
items.tooltip: For snug supports, the support regions will be merged using morphological closing operation. Gaps smaller than the closing radius will be filled in.

items.name: support_material_contact_distance
items.label: Top contact Z distance
items.tooltip: The vertical distance between object and support material interface. Setting this to 0 will also prevent Slic3r from using bridge flow and speed for the first object layer.

items.name: support_material_enforce_layers
items.label: Enforce support for the first
items.full_label: Enforce support for the first n layers
items.tooltip: Generate support material for the specified number of layers counting from bottom, regardless of whether normal support material is enabled or not and regardless of any angle threshold. This is useful for getting more adhesion of objects having a very thin or poor footprint on the build plate.

items.name: support_material_extruder
items.label: Support material/raft/skirt extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing support material, raft and skirt (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes).

items.name: support_material_extrusion_width
items.label: Support material
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for support material. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: support_material_first_layer_density
items.label: First layer density
items.tooltip: Density of the first support layer.

items.name: support_material_first_layer_expansion
items.label: First layer expansion
items.tooltip: Expansion of the support first layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

items.name: support_material_interface_contact_loops
items.label: Interface loops
items.tooltip: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.

items.name: support_material_interface_extruder
items.label: Support material/raft interface extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing support material interface (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes). This affects raft too.

items.name: support_material_interface_layers
items.label: Top interface layers
items.tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material.

items.name: support_material_interface_pattern
items.label: Interface pattern
items.tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

items.name: support_material_interface_spacing
items.label: Interface pattern spacing
items.tooltip: Spacing between interface lines. Set zero to get a solid interface.

items.name: support_material_interface_speed
items.label: Support material interface
items.tooltip: Speed for printing support material interface layers. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%) it will be calculated over support material speed.

items.name: support_material_pattern
items.label: Pattern
items.tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material.

items.name: support_material_spacing
items.label: Pattern spacing
items.tooltip: Spacing between support material lines.

items.name: support_material_speed
items.label: Support material
items.tooltip: Speed for printing support material.

items.name: support_material_style
items.label: Style
items.tooltip: Style and shape of the support towers. Projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports, while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.

items.name: support_material_synchronize_layers
items.label: Synchronize with object layers
items.tooltip: Synchronize support layers with the object print layers. This is useful with multi-material printers, where the extruder switch is expensive. This option is only available when top contact Z distance is set to zero.

items.name: support_material_threshold
items.label: Overhang threshold
items.tooltip: Support material will not be generated for overhangs whose slope angle (90° = vertical) is above the given threshold. In other words, this value represent the most horizontal slope (measured from the horizontal plane) that you can print without support material. Set to zero for automatic detection (recommended).

items.name: support_material_with_sheath
items.label: With sheath around the support
items.tooltip: Add a sheath (a single perimeter line) around the base support. This makes the support more reliable, but also more difficult to remove.

items.name: support_material_xy_spacing
items.label: XY separation between an object and its support
items.tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%), it will be calculated over external perimeter width.

items.name: support_tree_angle
items.label: Maximum Branch Angle
items.tooltip: The maximum angle of the branches, when the branches have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

items.name: support_tree_angle_slow
items.label: Preferred Branch Angle
items.tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

items.name: support_tree_branch_diameter
items.label: Branch Diameter
items.tooltip: The diameter of the thinnest branches of organic support. Thicker branches are more sturdy. Branches towards the base will be thicker than this.

items.name: support_tree_branch_diameter_angle
items.label: Branch Diameter Angle
items.tooltip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

items.name: support_tree_branch_diameter_double_wall
items.label: Branch Diameter with double walls
items.tooltip: Branches with area larger than the area of a circle of this diameter will be printed with double walls for stability. Set this value to zero for no double walls.

items.name: support_tree_branch_distance
items.label: Branch Distance
items.tooltip: How far apart the branches need to be when they touch the model. Making this distance small will cause the tree support to touch the model at more points, causing better overhang but making support harder to remove.

items.name: support_tree_tip_diameter
items.label: Tip Diameter
items.tooltip: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

items.name: support_tree_top_rate
items.label: Branch Density
items.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

items.name: thick_bridges
items.label: Thick bridges
items.tooltip: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

items.name: thin_walls
items.label: Detect thin walls
items.tooltip: Detect single-width walls (parts where two extrusions don't fit and we need to collapse them into a single trace).

items.name: toolchange_ordering
items.label: Toolchange ordering
items.tooltip:
Determines the order of tool changes on each layer.
Optimized - Starts with the last used extruder to minimize tool changes.
Cyclic - Uses extruders in a fixed sequential order (1, 2, 3, ...) on every layer.

items.name: top_fill_pattern
items.label: Top fill pattern
items.tooltip: Fill pattern for top infill. This only affects the top visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

items.name: top_infill_extrusion_width
items.label: Top solid infill
items.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for top surfaces. You may want to use thinner extrudates to fill all narrow regions and get a smoother finish. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

items.name: top_one_perimeter_type
items.label: Single perimeter on top surfaces
items.tooltip: Use only one perimeter on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern. Could be applied on topmost surface or all top surfaces.

items.name: top_solid_infill_acceleration
items.label: Top solid infill
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for top solid infill. Set zero to use the value for solid infill.

items.name: top_solid_infill_speed
items.label: Top solid infill
items.tooltip: Speed for printing top solid layers (it only applies to the uppermost external layers and not to their internal solid layers). You may want to slow down this to get a nicer surface finish. This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the solid infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

items.name: top_solid_layers
items.label: Top solid layers
items.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on top surfaces.

items.name: top_solid_min_thickness
items.label: Minimum top shell thickness
items.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased above top_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of top shell. This is useful to prevent pillowing effect when printing with variable layer height.

items.name: travel_acceleration
items.label: Travel
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for travel moves. Set zero to disable acceleration control for travel.

items.name: travel_lift_before_obstacle
items.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
items.tooltip: If enabled, PrusaSlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

items.name: travel_max_lift
items.label: Maximum ramping lift
items.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

items.name: travel_ramping_lift
items.label: Use ramping lift
items.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

items.name: travel_short_distance_acceleration
items.label: Travel short distance acceleration
items.tooltip: Acceleration used for short travel moves. Short travel distance is determined by the retract_before_travel setting.

items.name: travel_slope
items.label: Ramping slope angle
items.tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

items.name: travel_speed
items.label: Travel
items.tooltip: Speed for travel moves (jumps between distant extrusion points).

items.name: travel_speed_z
items.label: Z travel
items.tooltip:
Speed for movements along the Z axis.
When set to zero, the value is ignored and regular travel speed is used instead.

items.name: wall_distribution_count
items.label: Perimeter distribution count
items.tooltip: The number of perimeters, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer perimeters don't change in width.

items.name: wall_transition_angle
items.label: Perimeter transitioning threshold angle
items.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of perimeters. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no perimeters will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center perimeters, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

items.name: wall_transition_filter_deviation
items.label: Perimeter transitioning filter margin
items.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra perimeter and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum perimeter width - margin, 2 * Minimum perimeter width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

items.name: wall_transition_length
items.label: Perimeter transition length
items.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of perimeters as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the perimeter segments. If expressed as a percentage (for example 100%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

items.name: wipe
items.label: Wipe while retracting
items.tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.

items.name: wipe_tower
items.label: Enable
items.tooltip: Multi material printers may need to prime or purge extruders on tool changes. Extrude the excess material into the wipe tower.

items.name: wipe_tower_acceleration
items.label: Wipe tower
items.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for wipe tower. Set zero to disable acceleration control for the wipe tower.

items.name: wipe_tower_bridging
items.label: Maximal bridging distance
items.tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

items.name: wipe_tower_brim_width
items.label: Wipe tower brim width
items.tooltip: Wipe tower brim width

items.name: wipe_tower_cone_angle
items.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
items.tooltip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

items.name: wipe_tower_extra_flow
items.label: Extra flow for purging
items.tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

items.name: wipe_tower_extra_spacing
items.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
items.tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

items.name: wipe_tower_extruder
items.label: Wipe tower extruder
items.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

items.name: wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers
items.label: No sparse layers (EXPERIMENTAL)
items.tooltip: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no toolchanges. On layers with a toolchange, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

items.name: wipe_tower_width
items.label: Width
items.tooltip: Width of a wipe tower

items.name: xy_size_compensation
items.label: XY Size Compensation
items.tooltip: The object will be grown/shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value (negative = inwards, positive = outwards). This might be useful for fine-tuning hole sizes.

overrides.name: automatic_infill_combination
overrides.label: Automatic infill combination
overrides.tooltip: This feature automatically combines infill of several layers and speeds up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus maintaining accuracy.

overrides.name: automatic_infill_combination_max_layer_height
overrides.label: Automatic infill combination - Max layer height
overrides.tooltip: Maximum layer height for combining infill when automatic infill combining is enabled. Maximum layer height could be specified either as an absolute in millimeters value or as a percentage of nozzle diameter. For printing with different nozzle diameters, it is recommended to use percentage value over absolute value.

overrides.name: bottom_solid_layers
overrides.label: Bottom solid layers
overrides.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on bottom surfaces.

overrides.name: bottom_solid_min_thickness
overrides.label: Minimum bottom shell thickness
overrides.tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased above bottom_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of bottom shell.

overrides.name: bridge_acceleration
overrides.label: Bridge
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for bridges. Set zero to disable acceleration control for bridges.

overrides.name: bridge_flow_ratio
overrides.label: Bridge flow ratio
overrides.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of plastic for bridging. You can decrease it slightly to pull the extrudates and prevent sagging, although default settings are usually good and you should experiment with cooling (use a fan) before tweaking this.

overrides.name: bridge_speed
overrides.label: Bridges
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing bridges.

overrides.name: brim_separation
overrides.label: Brim separation gap
overrides.tooltip: Offset of brim from the printed object. The offset is applied after the elephant foot compensation.

overrides.name: default_acceleration
overrides.label: Default
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will be reset to after the role-specific acceleration values are used (perimeter/infill). Set zero to prevent resetting acceleration at all.

overrides.name: deretract_speed
overrides.label: Deretraction Speed
overrides.tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

overrides.name: dont_support_bridges
overrides.label: Don't support bridges
overrides.tooltip: Experimental option for preventing support material from being generated under bridged areas.

overrides.name: elefant_foot_compensation
overrides.label: Elephant foot compensation
overrides.tooltip: The first layer will be shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value to compensate for the 1st layer squish aka an Elephant Foot effect.

overrides.name: enable_dynamic_overhang_speeds
overrides.label: Enable dynamic overhang speeds
overrides.tooltip: This setting enables dynamic speed control on overhangs.

overrides.name: external_perimeter_acceleration
overrides.label: External perimeters
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for external perimeters. Set zero to use the value for perimeters.

overrides.name: external_perimeter_extrusion_width
overrides.label: External perimeters
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for external perimeters. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%), it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: external_perimeter_speed
overrides.label: External perimeters
overrides.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of external perimeters (the visible ones). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

overrides.name: external_perimeters_first
overrides.label: External perimeters first
overrides.tooltip: Print contour perimeters from the outermost one to the innermost one instead of the default inverse order.

overrides.name: extra_perimeters
overrides.label: Extra perimeters if needed
overrides.tooltip: Add more perimeters when needed for avoiding gaps in sloping walls. Slic3r keeps adding perimeters, until more than 70% of the loop immediately above is supported.

overrides.name: extra_perimeters_on_overhangs
overrides.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs (Experimental)
overrides.tooltip: Detect overhang areas where bridges cannot be anchored, and fill them with extra perimeter paths. These paths are anchored to the nearby non-overhang area when possible.

overrides.name: extrusion_width
overrides.label: Default extrusion width
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to allow a manual extrusion width. If left to zero, Slic3r derives extrusion widths from the nozzle diameter (see the tooltips for perimeter extrusion width, infill extrusion width etc). If expressed as percentage (for example: 230%), it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: fill_density
overrides.label: Fill density
overrides.tooltip: Density of internal infill, expressed in the range 0% - 100%.

overrides.name: fill_pattern
overrides.label: Fill pattern
overrides.tooltip: Fill pattern for general low-density infill.

overrides.name: first_layer_acceleration
overrides.label: First layer
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer.

overrides.name: first_layer_acceleration_over_raft
overrides.label: First object layer over raft interface
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer of object above raft interface. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer of object above raft interface.

overrides.name: first_layer_external_perimeter_speed
overrides.label: First layer perimeter speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the external perimeter print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the external perimeter speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: first_layer_extrusion_width
overrides.label: First layer
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for first layer. You can use this to force fatter extrudates for better adhesion. If expressed as percentage (for example 120%) it will be computed over nozzle_diameter. If set to zero, it will use the default extrusion width.

overrides.name: first_layer_gap_fill_speed
overrides.label: First layer gap fill speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any gap fill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the gap fill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: first_layer_height
overrides.label: First layer height
overrides.tooltip: When printing with very low layer heights, you might still want to print a thicker bottom layer to improve adhesion and tolerance for non perfect build plates.

overrides.name: first_layer_infill_speed
overrides.label: First layer infill speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: first_layer_perimeter_speed
overrides.label: First layer perimeter speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the perimeter print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the perimeter speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: first_layer_solid_infill_speed
overrides.label: First layer solid infill speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the solid infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the solid infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: first_layer_speed
overrides.label: First layer speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first layer, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

overrides.name: first_layer_speed_over_raft
overrides.label: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first object layer above raft interface, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

overrides.name: first_layer_support_material_speed
overrides.label: First layer support material speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any support print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the support material speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: first_layer_top_solid_infill_speed
overrides.label: First layer top solid infill speed
overrides.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any top solid print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the top solid infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

overrides.name: gap_fill_enabled
overrides.label: Fill gaps
overrides.tooltip: Enables filling of gaps between perimeters and between the inner most perimeters and infill.

overrides.name: gap_fill_speed
overrides.label: Gap fill
overrides.tooltip: Speed for filling small gaps using short zigzag moves. Keep this reasonably low to avoid too much shaking and resonance issues. Set zero to disable gaps filling.

overrides.name: gcode_resolution
overrides.label: G-code resolution
overrides.tooltip: Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts. Very high resolution G-code requires huge amount of RAM to slice and preview, also a 3D printer may stutter not being able to process a high resolution G-code in a timely manner. On the other hand, a low resolution G-code will produce a low poly effect and because the G-code reduction is performed at each layer independently, visible artifacts may be produced.

overrides.name: infill_acceleration
overrides.label: Infill
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for infill. Set zero to disable acceleration control for infill.

overrides.name: infill_anchor
overrides.label: Length of the infill anchor
overrides.tooltip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. PrusaSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

overrides.name: infill_anchor_max
overrides.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
overrides.tooltip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. PrusaSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring.

overrides.name: infill_every_layers
overrides.label: Combine infill every
overrides.tooltip: This feature allows to combine infill and speed up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus accuracy.

overrides.name: infill_extrusion_width
overrides.label: Infill
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used.
