You may want to use fatter extrudates to speed up the infill and make your parts stronger. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: infill_overlap
overrides.label: Infill/perimeters overlap
overrides.tooltip: This setting applies an additional overlap between infill and perimeters for better bonding. Theoretically this shouldn't be needed, but backlash might cause gaps. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over perimeter extrusion width.

overrides.name: infill_speed
overrides.label: Infill
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing the internal fill. Set to zero for auto.

overrides.name: max_layer_height
overrides.label: Max
overrides.tooltip: This is the highest printable layer height for this extruder, used to cap the variable layer height and support layer height. Maximum recommended layer height is 75% of the extrusion width to achieve reasonable inter-layer adhesion. If set to 0, layer height is limited to 75% of the nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: max_print_speed
overrides.label: Max print speed
overrides.tooltip: When setting other speed settings to 0 Slic3r will autocalculate the optimal speed in order to keep constant extruder pressure. This experimental setting is used to set the highest print speed you want to allow.

overrides.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_negative
overrides.label: Max volumetric slope negative
overrides.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from higher speed to lower speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 5.4 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 60 mm/s) to 1.8 mm³/s (feedrate 20 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

overrides.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_positive
overrides.label: Max volumetric slope positive
overrides.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from lower speed to higher speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 1.8 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 20 mm/s) to 5.4 mm³/s (feedrate 60 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

overrides.name: max_volumetric_speed
overrides.label: Max volumetric speed
overrides.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to set the maximum volumetric speed your extruder supports.

overrides.name: min_bead_width
overrides.label: Minimum perimeter width
overrides.tooltip: Width of the perimeter that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum perimeter width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the perimeter will become as thick as the feature itself. If expressed as a percentage (for example 85%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: min_feature_size
overrides.label: Minimum feature size
overrides.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum perimeter width. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the biggest nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: min_layer_height
overrides.label: Min
overrides.tooltip: This is the lowest printable layer height for this extruder and limits the resolution for variable layer height. Typical values are between 0.05 mm and 0.1 mm.

overrides.name: only_one_perimeter_first_layer
overrides.label: Only one perimeter on first layer
overrides.tooltip: Use only one perimeter on the first layer.

overrides.name: only_retract_when_crossing_perimeters
overrides.label: Only retract when crossing perimeters
overrides.tooltip: Disables retraction when the travel path does not exceed the upper layer's perimeters (and thus any ooze will be probably invisible).

overrides.name: over_bridge_speed
overrides.label: Over bridges
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing solid infill above bridges. Set to 0 to use solid infill speed. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over solid infill speed.

overrides.name: overhang_speed_0
overrides.label: speed for 0% overlap (bridge)
overrides.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

overrides.name: overhang_speed_1
overrides.label: speed for 25% overlap
overrides.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

overrides.name: overhang_speed_2
overrides.label: speed for 50% overlap
overrides.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

overrides.name: overhang_speed_3
overrides.label: speed for 75% overlap
overrides.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

overrides.name: overhangs
overrides.label: Detect bridging perimeters
overrides.tooltip: Experimental option to adjust flow for overhangs (bridge flow will be used), to apply bridge speed to them and enable fan.

overrides.name: perimeter_acceleration
overrides.label: Perimeters
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for perimeters. Set zero to disable acceleration control for perimeters.

overrides.name: perimeter_extrusion_width
overrides.label: Perimeters
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for perimeters. You may want to use thinner extrudates to get more accurate surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: perimeter_speed
overrides.label: Perimeters
overrides.tooltip: Speed for perimeters (contours, aka vertical shells). Set to zero for auto.

overrides.name: perimeters
overrides.label: Perimeters
overrides.tooltip: This option sets the minimal number of perimeters to generate for each layer. Note that Slic3r may increase this number automatically when it detects sloping surfaces which benefit from a higher number of perimeters if the Extra Perimeters option is enabled.

overrides.name: raft_contact_distance
overrides.label: Raft contact Z distance
overrides.tooltip: The vertical distance between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface.

overrides.name: raft_expansion
overrides.label: Raft expansion
overrides.tooltip: Expansion of the raft in XY plane for better stability.

overrides.name: raft_first_layer_density
overrides.label: First layer density
overrides.tooltip: Density of the first raft layer.

overrides.name: raft_first_layer_expansion
overrides.label: Raft first layer expansion
overrides.tooltip: Expansion of the raft first layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

overrides.name: retract_before_travel
overrides.label: Minimum travel after retraction
overrides.tooltip: Retraction is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

overrides.name: retract_before_wipe
overrides.label: Retract amount before wipe
overrides.tooltip: With bowden extruders, it may be wise to do some amount of quick retract before doing the wipe movement.

overrides.name: retract_layer_change
overrides.label: Retract on layer change
overrides.tooltip: This flag enforces a retraction whenever a Z move is done.

overrides.name: retract_length
overrides.label: Retraction length
overrides.tooltip: When retraction is triggered, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

overrides.name: retract_length_toolchange
overrides.label: Length
overrides.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

overrides.name: retract_lift
overrides.label: Lift height
overrides.tooltip: Lift height applied before travel.

overrides.name: retract_lift_above
overrides.label: Only lift Above Z
overrides.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for skipping lift on the first layers.

overrides.name: retract_lift_below
overrides.label: Only lift Below Z
overrides.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for limiting lift to the first layers.

overrides.name: retract_restart_extra
overrides.label: Deretraction extra length
overrides.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

overrides.name: retract_restart_extra_toolchange
overrides.label: Extra length on restart
overrides.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

overrides.name: retract_speed
overrides.label: Retraction Speed
overrides.tooltip: The speed for retractions (it only applies to the extruder motor).

overrides.name: seam_position
overrides.label: Seam position
overrides.tooltip: Position of perimeters starting points.

overrides.name: small_perimeter_speed
overrides.label: Small perimeters
overrides.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= 6.5mm (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

overrides.name: solid_infill_acceleration
overrides.label: Solid infill
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for solid infill. Set zero to use the value for infill.

overrides.name: solid_infill_extrusion_width
overrides.label: Solid infill
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for solid surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: solid_infill_speed
overrides.label: Solid infill
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing solid regions (top/bottom/internal horizontal shells). This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the default infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

overrides.name: support_material_angle
overrides.label: Pattern angle
overrides.tooltip: Use this setting to rotate the support material pattern on the horizontal plane.

overrides.name: support_material_bottom_contact_distance
overrides.label: Bottom contact Z distance
overrides.tooltip: The vertical distance between the object top surface and the support material interface. If set to zero, support_material_contact_distance will be used for both top and bottom contact Z distances.

overrides.name: support_material_bottom_interface_layers
overrides.label: Bottom interface layers
overrides.tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material. Set to -1 to use support_material_interface_layers

overrides.name: support_material_closing_radius
overrides.label: Closing radius
overrides.tooltip: For snug supports, the support regions will be merged using morphological closing operation. Gaps smaller than the closing radius will be filled in.

overrides.name: support_material_contact_distance
overrides.label: Top contact Z distance
overrides.tooltip: The vertical distance between object and support material interface. Setting this to 0 will also prevent Slic3r from using bridge flow and speed for the first object layer.

overrides.name: support_material_enforce_layers
overrides.label: Enforce support for the first
overrides.full_label: Enforce support for the first n layers
overrides.tooltip: Generate support material for the specified number of layers counting from bottom, regardless of whether normal support material is enabled or not and regardless of any angle threshold. This is useful for getting more adhesion of objects having a very thin or poor footprint on the build plate.

overrides.name: support_material_extrusion_width
overrides.label: Support material
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for support material. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: support_material_first_layer_density
overrides.label: First layer density
overrides.tooltip: Density of the first support layer.

overrides.name: support_material_first_layer_expansion
overrides.label: First layer expansion
overrides.tooltip: Expansion of the support first layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

overrides.name: support_material_interface_contact_loops
overrides.label: Interface loops
overrides.tooltip: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.

overrides.name: support_material_interface_layers
overrides.label: Top interface layers
overrides.tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material.

overrides.name: support_material_interface_pattern
overrides.label: Interface pattern
overrides.tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

overrides.name: support_material_interface_spacing
overrides.label: Interface pattern spacing
overrides.tooltip: Spacing between interface lines. Set zero to get a solid interface.

overrides.name: support_material_interface_speed
overrides.label: Support material interface
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing support material interface layers. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%) it will be calculated over support material speed.

overrides.name: support_material_pattern
overrides.label: Pattern
overrides.tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material.

overrides.name: support_material_spacing
overrides.label: Pattern spacing
overrides.tooltip: Spacing between support material lines.

overrides.name: support_material_speed
overrides.label: Support material
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing support material.

overrides.name: support_material_style
overrides.label: Style
overrides.tooltip: Style and shape of the support towers. Projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports, while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.

overrides.name: support_material_synchronize_layers
overrides.label: Synchronize with object layers
overrides.tooltip: Synchronize support layers with the object print layers. This is useful with multi-material printers, where the extruder switch is expensive. This option is only available when top contact Z distance is set to zero.

overrides.name: support_material_threshold
overrides.label: Overhang threshold
overrides.tooltip: Support material will not be generated for overhangs whose slope angle (90° = vertical) is above the given threshold. In other words, this value represent the most horizontal slope (measured from the horizontal plane) that you can print without support material. Set to zero for automatic detection (recommended).

overrides.name: support_material_with_sheath
overrides.label: With sheath around the support
overrides.tooltip: Add a sheath (a single perimeter line) around the base support. This makes the support more reliable, but also more difficult to remove.

overrides.name: support_material_xy_spacing
overrides.label: XY separation between an object and its support
overrides.tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%), it will be calculated over external perimeter width.

overrides.name: support_tree_angle
overrides.label: Maximum Branch Angle
overrides.tooltip: The maximum angle of the branches, when the branches have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

overrides.name: support_tree_angle_slow
overrides.label: Preferred Branch Angle
overrides.tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

overrides.name: support_tree_branch_diameter
overrides.label: Branch Diameter
overrides.tooltip: The diameter of the thinnest branches of organic support. Thicker branches are more sturdy. Branches towards the base will be thicker than this.

overrides.name: support_tree_branch_diameter_angle
overrides.label: Branch Diameter Angle
overrides.tooltip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

overrides.name: support_tree_branch_diameter_double_wall
overrides.label: Branch Diameter with double walls
overrides.tooltip: Branches with area larger than the area of a circle of this diameter will be printed with double walls for stability. Set this value to zero for no double walls.

overrides.name: support_tree_branch_distance
overrides.label: Branch Distance
overrides.tooltip: How far apart the branches need to be when they touch the model. Making this distance small will cause the tree support to touch the model at more points, causing better overhang but making support harder to remove.

overrides.name: support_tree_tip_diameter
overrides.label: Tip Diameter
overrides.tooltip: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

overrides.name: support_tree_top_rate
overrides.label: Branch Density
overrides.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

overrides.name: thick_bridges
overrides.label: Thick bridges
overrides.tooltip: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

overrides.name: toolchange_ordering
overrides.label: Toolchange ordering
overrides.tooltip:
Determines the order of tool changes on each layer.
Optimized - Starts with the last used extruder to minimize tool changes.
Cyclic - Uses extruders in a fixed sequential order (1, 2, 3, ...) on every layer.

overrides.name: top_infill_extrusion_width
overrides.label: Top solid infill
overrides.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for top surfaces. You may want to use thinner extrudates to fill all narrow regions and get a smoother finish. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: top_one_perimeter_type
overrides.label: Single perimeter on top surfaces
overrides.tooltip: Use only one perimeter on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern. Could be applied on topmost surface or all top surfaces.

overrides.name: top_solid_infill_acceleration
overrides.label: Top solid infill
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for top solid infill. Set zero to use the value for solid infill.

overrides.name: top_solid_infill_speed
overrides.label: Top solid infill
overrides.tooltip: Speed for printing top solid layers (it only applies to the uppermost external layers and not to their internal solid layers). You may want to slow down this to get a nicer surface finish. This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the solid infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

overrides.name: top_solid_layers
overrides.label: Top solid layers
overrides.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on top surfaces.

overrides.name: top_solid_min_thickness
overrides.label: Minimum top shell thickness
overrides.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased above top_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of top shell. This is useful to prevent pillowing effect when printing with variable layer height.

overrides.name: travel_acceleration
overrides.label: Travel
overrides.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for travel moves. Set zero to disable acceleration control for travel.

overrides.name: travel_lift_before_obstacle
overrides.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
overrides.tooltip: If enabled, PrusaSlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

overrides.name: travel_max_lift
overrides.label: Maximum ramping lift
overrides.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

overrides.name: travel_ramping_lift
overrides.label: Use ramping lift
overrides.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

overrides.name: travel_short_distance_acceleration
overrides.label: Travel short distance acceleration
overrides.tooltip: Acceleration used for short travel moves. Short travel distance is determined by the retract_before_travel setting.

overrides.name: travel_slope
overrides.label: Ramping slope angle
overrides.tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

overrides.name: travel_speed
overrides.label: Travel
overrides.tooltip: Speed for travel moves (jumps between distant extrusion points).

overrides.name: travel_speed_z
overrides.label: Z travel
overrides.tooltip:
Speed for movements along the Z axis.
When set to zero, the value is ignored and regular travel speed is used instead.

overrides.name: wall_distribution_count
overrides.label: Perimeter distribution count
overrides.tooltip: The number of perimeters, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer perimeters don't change in width.

overrides.name: wall_transition_angle
overrides.label: Perimeter transitioning threshold angle
overrides.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of perimeters. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no perimeters will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center perimeters, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

overrides.name: wall_transition_filter_deviation
overrides.label: Perimeter transitioning filter margin
overrides.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra perimeter and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum perimeter width - margin, 2 * Minimum perimeter width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: wall_transition_length
overrides.label: Perimeter transition length
overrides.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of perimeters as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the perimeter segments. If expressed as a percentage (for example 100%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

overrides.name: wipe
overrides.label: Wipe while retracting
overrides.tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.

overrides.name: wipe_tower_bridging
overrides.label: Maximal bridging distance
overrides.tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

overrides.name: wipe_tower_extra_flow
overrides.label: Extra flow for purging
overrides.tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

overrides.name: wipe_tower_extra_spacing
overrides.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
overrides.tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

items.name: bed_temperature
items.label: Bed other layers
items.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers after the first one. Set this to zero to disable bed temperature control commands in the output.

items.name: bridge_fan_speed
items.label: Bridges fan speed
items.tooltip: This fan speed is enforced during all bridges and overhangs.

items.name: chamber_minimal_temperature
items.label: Chamber Minimal temperature
items.tooltip:
Minimal chamber temperature that the printer waits for before the print starts. This allows to start the print before the nominal chamber temperature is reached.
When set to zero, the minimal chamber temperature is not set in the G-code.

items.name: chamber_temperature
items.label: Chamber Nominal temperature
items.tooltip:
Required chamber temperature for the print.
When set to zero, the nominal chamber temperature is not set in the G-code.

items.name: cooling
items.label: Enable auto cooling
items.tooltip: This flag enables the automatic cooling logic that adjusts print speed and fan speed according to layer printing time.

items.name: cooling_perimeter_transition_distance
items.label: Perimeter transition distance
items.tooltip: Distance in millimeters before non-slowed perimeters where the original unslowed print speed is restored. This reduces print quality issues when transitioning from heavily slowed feature to fast perimeter printing.

items.name: cooling_slowdown_logic
items.label: Cooling slowdown logic
items.tooltip: Determines how the printer slows down layer printing when the minimum layer time isn't reached. 'Consistent surface' first tries to preserve the print speeds of the first two perimeters by slowing all other features. Only if this isn't sufficient, it also slows down those first two perimeters. 'Uniform cooling' slows down all print features, including the first two perimeters.

items.name: custom_parameters_filament
items.label: Custom filament parameters
items.tooltip:
JSON-encoded string defining extra parameters, which can later be expanded in Custom G-code macro language. Each of the parameters is prepended by custom_parameter_filament prefix before it is passed into the parser. For example, defining '{"my_key": "my_value"}' allows to use 'custom_parameter_filament_my_key'.

The JSON must be single level (no arrays and objects). All value types are allowed, but nulls will be rejected by the parser.

items.name: disable_fan_first_layers
items.label: Disable fan for the first
items.tooltip: You can set this to a positive value to disable fan at all during the first layers, so that it does not make adhesion worse.

items.name: enable_dynamic_fan_speeds
items.label: Enable dynamic fan speeds
items.tooltip: This setting enables dynamic fan speed control on overhangs.

items.name: end_filament_gcode
items.label: End G-code
items.tooltip: This end procedure is inserted at the end of the output file, before the printer end gcode (and before any toolchange from this filament in case of multimaterial printers). Note that you can use placeholder variables for all PrusaSlicer settings. If you have multiple extruders, the gcode is processed in extruder order.
items.value:
; Filament-specific end gcode 
;END gcode for filament

items.name: extrusion_multiplier
items.label: Extrusion multiplier
items.tooltip: This factor changes the amount of flow proportionally. You may need to tweak this setting to get nice surface finish and correct single wall widths. Usual values are between 0.9 and 1.1. If you think you need to change this more, check filament diameter and your firmware E steps.

items.name: fan_always_on
items.label: Keep fan always on
items.tooltip: If this is enabled, fan will never be disabled and will be kept running at least at its minimum speed. Useful for PLA, harmful for ABS.

items.name: fan_below_layer_time
items.label: Enable fan if layer print time is below
items.tooltip: If layer print time is estimated below this number of seconds, fan will be enabled and its speed will be calculated by interpolating the minimum and maximum speeds.

items.name: filament_abrasive
items.label: Abrasive material
items.tooltip: This flag means that the material is abrasive and requires a hardened nozzle. The value is used by the printer to check it.

items.name: filament_colour
items.label: Color
items.tooltip: Leave unused if the filament profile isn't tied to a specific color. Color can still be set at project-level.

items.name: filament_cooling_final_speed
items.label: Speed of the last cooling move
items.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

items.name: filament_cooling_initial_speed
items.label: Speed of the first cooling move
items.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

items.name: filament_cooling_moves
items.label: Number of cooling moves
items.tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

items.name: filament_cost
items.label: Cost
items.tooltip: Enter your filament cost per kg here. This is only for statistical information.

items.name: filament_density
items.label: Density
items.tooltip: Enter your filament density here. This is only for statistical information. A decent way is to weigh a known length of filament and compute the ratio of the length to volume. Better is to calculate the volume directly through displacement.

items.name: filament_diameter
items.label: Diameter
items.tooltip: Enter your filament diameter here. Good precision is required, so use a caliper and do multiple measurements along the filament, then compute the average.

items.name: filament_flush_speed
items.label: Flush speed
items.tooltip: Extrusion speed used for flushing during a tool change. Used in custom toolchange G-code.

items.name: filament_flush_volume
items.label: Flush volume
items.tooltip: Volume of filament to flush during a tool change. Used in custom toolchange G-code.

items.name: filament_infill_max_crossing_speed
items.label: Max crossing infill speed
items.tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill with self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

items.name: filament_infill_max_speed
items.label: Max non-crossing infill speed
items.tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill without any self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

items.name: filament_loading_speed
items.label: Loading speed
items.tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

items.name: filament_loading_speed_start
items.label: Loading speed at the start
items.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

items.name: filament_max_volumetric_speed
items.label: Max volumetric speed
items.tooltip: Maximum volumetric speed allowed for this filament. Limits the maximum volumetric speed of a print to the minimum of print and filament volumetric speed. Set to zero for no limit.

items.name: filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower
items.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
items.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Slic3r will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

items.name: filament_multitool_ramming
items.label: Enable ramming for multitool setups
items.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multitool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the toolchange. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

items.name: filament_multitool_ramming_flow
items.label: Multitool ramming flow
items.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the toolchange.

items.name: filament_multitool_ramming_volume
items.label: Multitool ramming volume
items.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the toolchange.

items.name: filament_notes
items.label: Filament notes
items.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

items.name: filament_purge_multiplier
items.label: Purge volume multiplier
items.tooltip: Purging volume on the wipe tower is determined by 'multimaterial_purging' in Printer Settings. This option allows to modify the volume on filament level. Note that the project can override this by setting project-specific values.

items.name: filament_ramming_initial_delay
items.label: Pause before ramming
items.tooltip: Time in seconds that the printer will remain idle before ramming, allowing the melt zone temperature to equalize.

items.name: filament_ramming_parameters
items.label: Ramming parameters
items.tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

items.name: filament_ramming_temperature_delta
items.label: Ramming temperature variation
items.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied right before ramming. The value can be negative.

items.name: filament_shrinkage_compensation_xy
items.label: Shrinkage compensation XY
items.tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentages for the X and Y axes here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the X and Y axes. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

items.name: filament_shrinkage_compensation_z
items.label: Shrinkage compensation Z
items.tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentages for the Z axis here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the Z axis. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

items.name: filament_soluble
items.label: Soluble material
items.tooltip: Soluble material is most likely used for a soluble support.

items.name: filament_spool_weight
items.label: Spool weight
items.tooltip: Enter weight of the empty filament spool. One may weigh a partially consumed filament spool before printing and one may compare the measured weight with the calculated weight of the filament with the spool to find out whether the amount of filament on the spool is sufficient to finish the print.

items.name: filament_stamping_distance
items.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
items.tooltip: If set to nonzero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

items.name: filament_stamping_loading_speed
items.label: Stamping loading speed
items.tooltip: Speed used for stamping.

items.name: filament_toolchange_delay
items.label: Delay after unloading
items.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable toolchanges with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

items.name: filament_type
items.label: Filament type
items.tooltip: The filament material type for use in custom G-codes.

items.name: filament_unloading_speed
items.label: Unloading speed
items.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect  initial part of unloading just after ramming).

items.name: filament_unloading_speed_start
items.label: Unloading speed at the start
items.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

items.name: first_layer_bed_temperature
items.label: Bed First layer
items.tooltip: Heated build plate temperature for the first layer. Set this to zero to disable bed temperature control commands in the output.

items.name: first_layer_temperature
items.label: Nozzle First layer
items.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for the first layer. If you want to control temperature manually during print, set this to zero to disable temperature control commands in the output G-code.

items.name: full_fan_speed_layer
items.label: Full fan speed at layer
items.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "disable_fan_first_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "disable_fan_first_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "disable_fan_first_layers" + 1.

items.name: idle_temperature
items.label: Idle temperature
items.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups.This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings.

items.name: max_fan_speed
items.label: Max Fan speed
items.tooltip: This setting represents the maximum speed of your fan.

items.name: min_fan_speed
items.label: Min fan speed
items.tooltip: This setting represents the minimum PWM your fan needs to work.

items.name: min_print_speed
items.label: Min print speed
items.tooltip: Slic3r will not scale speed down below this speed.

items.name: overhang_fan_speed_0
items.label: speed for 0% overlap (bridge)
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Fan speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation.

items.name: overhang_fan_speed_1
items.label: speed for 25% overlap
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Fan speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation.

items.name: overhang_fan_speed_2
items.label: speed for 50% overlap
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Fan speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation.

items.name: overhang_fan_speed_3
items.label: speed for 75% overlap
items.tooltip: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Fan speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation.

items.name: pressure_advance
items.label: Pressure advance
items.tooltip: Controls how the pressure advance value is emitted into g-code for this filament. 'Disabled' does not emit any pressure advance command, leaving the printer to use the pressure advance value set in the filament's start g-code (or the firmware default). 'Enabled' emits the configured pressure advance value. 'Automatic Calibration' emits the configured pressure advance value and then triggers the firmware's automatic pressure advance calibration.

items.name: pressure_advance_value
items.label: Pressure advance
items.tooltip: Pressure Advance (also called Linear Advance in some firmware) compensates for nozzle pressure to achieve sharper corners. Proper value helps reduce bulging on deceleration and under-extrusion on acceleration.

items.name: slowdown_below_layer_time
items.label: Slow down if layer print time is below
items.tooltip: If layer print time is estimated below this number of seconds, print moves speed will be scaled down to extend duration to this value.

items.name: start_filament_gcode
items.label: Start G-code
items.tooltip: This start procedure is inserted at the beginning, after any printer start gcode (and after any toolchange to this filament in case of multi-material printers). This is used to override settings for a specific filament. If PrusaSlicer detects M104, M109, M140 or M190 in your custom codes, such commands will not be prepended automatically so you're free to customize the order of heating commands and other custom actions. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all PrusaSlicer settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want. If you have multiple extruders, the gcode is processed in extruder order.

items.name: temperature
items.label: Nozzle other layers
items.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for layers after the first one. Set this to zero to disable temperature control commands in the output G-code.

overrides.name: deretract_speed
overrides.label: Deretraction Speed
overrides.tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

overrides.name: retract_before_travel
overrides.label: Minimum travel after retraction
overrides.tooltip: Retraction is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

overrides.name: retract_before_wipe
overrides.label: Retract amount before wipe
overrides.tooltip: With bowden extruders, it may be wise to do some amount of quick retract before doing the wipe movement.

overrides.name: retract_layer_change
overrides.label: Retract on layer change
overrides.tooltip: This flag enforces a retraction whenever a Z move is done.

overrides.name: retract_length
overrides.label: Retraction length
overrides.tooltip: When retraction is triggered, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

overrides.name: retract_length_toolchange
overrides.label: Length
overrides.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

overrides.name: retract_lift
overrides.label: Lift height
overrides.tooltip: Lift height applied before travel.

overrides.name: retract_lift_above
overrides.label: Only lift Above Z
overrides.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for skipping lift on the first layers.

overrides.name: retract_lift_below
overrides.label: Only lift Below Z
overrides.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for limiting lift to the first layers.

overrides.name: retract_restart_extra
overrides.label: Deretraction extra length
overrides.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

overrides.name: retract_restart_extra_toolchange
overrides.label: Extra length on restart
overrides.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

overrides.name: retract_speed
overrides.label: Retraction Speed
overrides.tooltip: The speed for retractions (it only applies to the extruder motor).

overrides.name: seam_gap_distance
overrides.label: Seam gap distance
overrides.tooltip: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.

overrides.name: travel_lift_before_obstacle
overrides.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
overrides.tooltip: If enabled, PrusaSlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

overrides.name: travel_max_lift
overrides.label: Maximum ramping lift
overrides.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

overrides.name: travel_ramping_lift
overrides.label: Use ramping lift
overrides.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

overrides.name: travel_slope
overrides.label: Ramping slope angle
overrides.tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

overrides.name: wipe
overrides.label: Wipe while retracting
overrides.tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.
